summary: Contractor accepted Okta invite but elevated console role remains pending due to delegated-approval queue not advancing
description:
Issue summary: A third-party contractor (email: j.mendez@contractor.example.com) accepted the Okta invitation and appears in the 'contractors/temp-infra' Okta group. Expected outcome is automatic mapping to the 'read-only-console' RBAC role for the internal-inventory-console. Actual outcome: user can SSO into the Console but receives 403 when accessing inventory routes; their role in Identity Service is recorded as 'pending_approval'.

Impact: Contractor cannot complete onboarding validation tasks. No customer-facing outage. Priority raised due to an active onboarding ticket and scheduled audit access review today.

Environment: prod (us-east). Affected service: internal-inventory-console and identity-service role-binding flow.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Invite contractor via Okta SCIM invite flow to group 'contractors/temp-infra'.
2) Contractor accepts invitation and completes account setup.
3) Attempt to access /inventory/dashboard in Console.

Observed behavior:
- Console SSO works (user can log in).
- Attempts to access inventory pages return 403/Forbidden.
- Identity Service user record shows attribute 'access_state: pending_approval' and 'approved_by: null'.
- Okta System Log entry: "Add User to Group: contractors/temp-infra - SUCCESS (actor: admin-bot)" at 2026-03-12T09:14:22Z.
- Identity API response when attempting to reapply role binding: 412 Conflict with message 'approval workflow already queued'.

Expected behavior: Group membership should trigger immediate RBAC mapping when contractor tier is configured for auto-approval, or surface a clear pending-approval ticket for manual approvers.

Investigation notes:
- Identity-service audit log shows a received webhook from Okta for group change at 2026-03-12T09:14:23Z; worker process enqueued job id=job-9981 to process mapping.
- job-9981 failed with error 'ApprovalQueueTimeoutError: no approver available' according to job worker logs. Worker retried 3 times and then marked job as waiting_for_approval.
- Delegated-approval service healthcheck at 2026-03-12T09:15:00Z returned 200, but the approvals queue inspector shows backlog=0 and approvers_on_call=[] (empty).
- Oncall rotation for delegated-approvers was recently moved from PagerDuty schedule 'identity-admins' to 'platform-admins' in last week's config change (PR referenced above). The delegated-approval service expects members in LDAP group 'identity-delegates' but the migration script didn't populate the group due to an API rate-limit error during the scheduled run.
- Workaround applied: Support manually approved the pending approval in identity admin UI for j.mendez@contractor.example.com at 2026-03-12T10:02:12Z; user immediately obtained 'read-only-console' role and reported access restored.

Logs/snippets: 
- Okta System Log: eventId=00u1abcXkAddGroup, actor=admin-bot, outcome=SUCCESS
- Identity-worker log excerpt: "Processing job job-9981 -> ApprovalQueueTimeoutError (no approver configured)"
- Identity API response when reapplying: HTTP/1.1 412 Conflict

Temporary workaround: Manual approval via Identity Admin UI restores access. Use checklist: identity-admin -> search user -> Approve pending mapping -> verify role assigned.

Longer-term fix suggestions:
1) Re-run migration to populate 'identity-delegates' group with the platform-admins schedule members and add retry/backoff to migration job.
2) Add alert when delegated-approval queue finds approvers_on_call == [].
3) Allow an emergency auto-approve policy for designated contractor tiers when backlog==0 and approval_window>X minutes (with audit entry).

Next steps / To do:
- Diego to validate migration logs and re-run population job (ETA 2026-03-14).
- SRE/Identity to add monitoring alert for empty approvers_on_call (owner: identity-oncall).
- Security to sign off on emergency auto-approve policy (owner: security-eng).

Resolution notes: Manual approval performed to restore access; root cause appears to be incomplete migration of approvers to the expected LDAP group after schedule change. No code changes required for immediate remediation.
